name: Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector
storyHook: Incoming transmission from Tranquility Base on the Moon. Hey there, Earth explorer! Apollo 11 astronauts left me behind in the grey lunar dust back in 1969. I do not have batteries, a computer, or even a single moving part. Yet every week, scientists on Earth fire super-powered green lasers across 238,000 miles of space straight at my 100 tiny mirrors! ZAP! I bounce that light right back home in two-and-a-half seconds. Thanks to me, NASA discovered that the Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth, about as fast as your fingernails grow!
scienceBreakthrough: Proved the Moon is drifting away from Earth at 3.8 cm per year and measured Earth-Moon distance to millimeter precision.

spaceMath.label: Laser Round-Trip
spaceMath.detail: Light speed to Moon and back

quiz.question: How long does a laser pulse take to travel from Earth to this reflector and back?
quiz.explanation: Light travels at 186,000 miles per second! A round-trip to the Moon and back takes about 2.5 seconds.

name: Surveyor 3
storyHook: BEEP-BOOP! Calling Earth from the Ocean of Storms! When I landed on the Moon in 1967, I thought I was going to sit alone in the freezing lunar dark forever. For 31 long months, nobody visited. Then THUMP, THUMP, THUMP! I heard footsteps! Two Apollo 12 astronauts walked right down into my crater, dusted me off, waved hello, and took my camera back to Earth! I proved that spacecraft and even tiny Earth microbes can survive years in harsh space weather!
scienceBreakthrough: Only robotic lander visited by humans on another world; tested how 2.5 years of lunar dust, vacuum, and radiation age spacecraft hardware.

spaceMath.label: Parts Returned
spaceMath.detail: TV camera and scoop brought home

quiz.question: Which Apollo crew walked over to visit Surveyor 3 in November 1969?
quiz.explanation: Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean landed within 180 meters of Surveyor 3!

name: Opportunity Rover (Oppy)
storyHook: Rover Opportunity reporting from Mars! When NASA built me, they gave me a 90-day warranty. Guess what? I kept rolling for nearly 15 Earth years! I climbed steep crater rims, survived freezing Martian winters, and drove over 28 miles across the red dust. Along the way, I found tiny mineral blueberries that proved liquid water once flowed on Mars! Then in 2018, a massive dust storm turned the Martian sky pitch black. My final message home was: My battery is low and it is getting dark. Do not worry, cadet, my tire tracks on Mars will last forever!
scienceBreakthrough: Discovered hematite blueberries and sulfate minerals proving liquid water once flowed across ancient Mars.

quiz.question: How long was Opportunity originally designed to last on Mars?
quiz.explanation: Opportunity was built for a 90-sol mission, but lasted over 5,100 sols!

name: InSight Lander
storyHook: Shhh, listen closely! This is the InSight Lander on Mars. While other rovers drove around looking at rocks, I stayed in one spot and put my ear to the ground to listen to the heartbeat of Mars! Using my ultra-sensitive seismometer, I felt over 1,300 rumbling marsquakes and meteorite crashes! Those vibrations helped scientists draw the very first 3D map of Mars deep liquid iron core. Red dust eventually covered my solar wings, so I am resting now, but I unlocked the secrets hidden miles beneath the Martian surface!
scienceBreakthrough: Measured over 1,300 marsquakes to map Mars crust, mantle, and liquid iron-nickel core for the first time.

quiz.question: What did InSight listen for beneath the surface of Mars?
quiz.explanation: InSight used its SEIS seismometer to detect over 1,300 marsquakes and meteorite impacts.

name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
storyHook: WHOOSH! SPINNING UP ROTORS AT 2,400 RPM! Hey Earth, it is Ingenuity, the first helicopter to ever fly on another planet! Everyone said flying on Mars was impossible because the air is 100 times thinner than Earth. Well, I proved them wrong! I was only supposed to make 5 test flights, and I ended up flying 72 times across Jezero Crater, scouting ahead for the Perseverance rover! Even though I broke a rotor tip on my final landing, I proved that future astronauts will be able to fly across alien worlds!
scienceBreakthrough: Achieved the first powered, controlled flight on another planet and scouted ahead for the Perseverance rover.

quiz.question: Why did Ingenuity have to spin its blades so fast on Mars?
quiz.explanation: Because Mars atmosphere has less than 1% the density of Earth air, blades must spin super fast to generate lift.

name: Voyager 1
storyHook: Transmission received from interstellar space over 15 billion miles from Earth. I am Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object in history! I launched in 1977, zoomed past giant Jupiter and ringed Saturn, and snapped the famous Pale Blue Dot photo of our tiny home planet. In 2012, I broke right through the edge of our Sun magnetic bubble into the space between the stars! Bolted to my side is the Golden Record, a time capsule carrying Earth music, whale songs, and greetings in 55 languages. I am still traveling through the dark ocean of stars, carrying humanity voice forever!
scienceBreakthrough: First spacecraft to cross the heliopause into interstellar space and capture the iconic Pale Blue Dot photo of Earth.

quiz.question: What famous record does Voyager 1 carry with sounds and greetings from Earth?
quiz.explanation: Voyager 1 carries the Golden Record, a time capsule of Earth sounds, music, and greetings.
